children: MSFT consolidated Copilot into one app integrating Word, Excel, PowerPoint. It adds Home (chat, meeting/docs/email review), Code (GitHub Copilot-powered low-code), and Autopilot in private preview.
Stifel upgraded Microsoft (MSFT) to Buy and raised its price target to $575, citing expected mid- to upper‑teens revenue growth from Azure and CoPilot, better expense efficiency and strong cash flow.
Microsoft (MSFT) shares rose after its latest quarterly earnings. Stock has climbed 33% since late July, recovering from earlier AI uncertainty; earnings cited as the main driver of gains.
Microsoft (MSFT) updated Chat pricing: basic Chat stays a flat per-user license; Cowork, Code and Autopilot moved to usage-based, metered charges for advanced features.
Microsoft (MSFT) expects Azure capacity increases and efficiency gains, plus a bigger contribution from its OpenAI partnership, to help meet rising cloud demand.
Microsoft (MSFT) shifts agentic pricing from per-seat to mixed seat+usage model, billing partly by agent workload so costs rise with higher consumption for intensive agentic services
Microsoft (MSFT) launched FinOps for AI to track AI usage and costs, enforce spending policies, route credit requests via approvals, and restrict model access by employee group for cost governance.
Microsoft (MSFT) updated Copilot as AI UI and governance. Traders should track paid-seat growth, agent usage, Azure consumption from Copilot workloads, and enterprise FinOps adoption as key metrics.
Goldman Sachs expects Microsoft (MSFT) to boost debt issuance to fund AI infrastructure, as hyperscalers’ gross debt issuance may reach ~$420B in 2027, up ~60% from 2026.
Microsoft (MSFT) will roll out Home and Code via the Frontier program soon; Autopilot enters private preview end of September; new FinOps tools for AI spend management will be released.
